out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: A written employee health policy was not observed during the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH A DIGITAL COPY OF THE FAIRFAX COUNTY EMPLOYEE ILLNESS AGREEMENT. ALL EMPLOYEES WILL READ AND SIGN A COPY. RETAIN FOR FUTURE INSPECTIONS.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH FAIRFAX COUNTY’S VOMIT AND DIARRHEA CLEAN UP PROCEDURES. RETAIN FOR FUTURE INSPECTIONS.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Air Gaps/Breaks
violations.observation: The end of the wastewater pipe of the sanitizer basin of the 3-compartment sink was observed below the flood rim of the floor drain.
violations.corrective_action: An air gap between the water supply inlet and the flood level rim of the plumbing fixture, equipment, or nonfood equipment shall be at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet and may not be less than one inch. PIC TEMPORARILY PROPED THE PIPE UP WITH A METAL CONTAINER. THE PIPE WAS NOW OBSERVED ABOVE THE FLOOD RIM. PIC SUBMITTED A MAINTENANCE REQUEST TO PERMANENTLY FIX THE PIPE.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) in the 2DWR prep top cooler (next to flat top); sliced tomatoes (51f), cooked mushrooms (47f); 2) in the glass display cooler; whole turkey breast (45f), whole roast beef (44f), whole prosciuttini (44f), whole capacola (44f), whole provolone (45f), whole Swiss (44f), cooked mushrooms (44f); 3) on the To-Go service line; sliced tomatoes (56f), shredded lettuce (50f). Tomatoes and lettuce from the To-Go line were taken out of a working cooler 1 hour prior.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED ALL OF THE AFOREMENTIONED FOODS FROM THE PREP TOP COOLER AND THE GLASS DISPLAY COOLER. PIC MOVED THE FOOD FROM THE TO-GO SERVICE LINE TO THE WALK IN TO COOL TO 41f.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: whole cheeses and whole deli meats in the walk-in refrigerator, tuna salad, chicken salad, and shredded lettuce.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS INSTRUCTED STAFF TO LABEL ALL FOODS WITH THE DATE IT WAS PREPARED IF IT IS BEING STORED FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS. SEE DATE MARKING HANDOUT.
